info.name: Keepiq Machine Secret-Store API Contract (secret-store-api v1)
info.description:
Executable cross-repo contract for the keepiq machine secret-store API (openspec change openconnector-secret-store-api, capability secret-store-api, apiVersion 1). This is the shared verification artifact the OpenConnector-side resolver — built in the openconnector repo with its own openspec change — is contract-tested against. Pin this collection alongside apiVersion.

WHAT IT LOCKS: the discovery document shape; the token endpoint's grant/assertion validation and brute-force throttling; name-addressable retrieval (404 / single envelope / 409-with-candidates); the doriath-machine-secret-v1 envelope (format, encryption block with suiteId+certificateFingerprint+scheme, ciphertext-only — never plaintext); ETag/304 + updated_since rotation polling; client-encrypted write-back (POST/PUT, no delete route); and strict own-vault 404 scoping.

ZERO-KNOWLEDGE (ADR-003): every secret read returns CIPHERTEXT only; write-back payloads arrive pre-encrypted to the application's own certificate. The server never sees plaintext. Assertions verify the ciphertext block contains only the named base64 fields and that no plaintext-capable field appears.

TWO RUN MODES:
  (a) UNAUTHENTICATED CONTRACT (always runnable, no seed): the discovery document, the token-endpoint negative cases (unsupported grant, missing assertion -> 400 with throttle), and the bearer-required rejection of /api/v1/app/secrets. These run in every CI invocation.
  (b) SEEDED MACHINE FLOW (token -> by-name -> envelope -> rotation -> write-back -> cross-vault 404): requires an approved application with a known private key. Provide seededAppId + seededPrivateKeyPem (PKCS#8 PEM) env vars; a pre-request script signs the RS256 JWT-bearer assertion. When the seed vars are absent the seeded requests skip their bodies honestly (pm.test.skip) — mirroring how the main keepiq collection quarantines in-browser crypto-minting flows. The openconnector-side CI provides the seed and runs the full flow.

AUTH MODEL: collection auth is noauth. Discovery + bearer-required tests target {{noAuthBase}} (127.0.0.1) so no NC session cookie leaks. Seeded requests carry an explicit Bearer header from the token exchange.

item.description: Requires seededAppId + seededPrivateKeyPem. Each request's pre-request script signs a fresh RS256 JWT-bearer assertion (aud='keepiq', exp=iat+120, unique jti) and exchanges it for the access token, then runs the contract assertions. When the seed vars are absent the assertions are skipped honestly so the unauthenticated subset still passes in seedless CI.

exec: // Prefer the assertion the RUNNER signed. Newman's sandbox has no node crypto
// module, so in-collection signing always failed and every seeded test below
// silently skipped — see the comment block in run-newman.sh.
// Sign an RS256 JWT-bearer assertion with the seeded private key.
// Requires the seed env vars; otherwise leave assertion empty and skip.
const payload = { iss: appId, aud: 'keepiq', iat: now, exp: now + 120, jti: 'newman-' + now + '-' + Math.random().toString(36).slice(2) };
// Signing uses node's crypto when run via newman (CryptoJS lacks RSA).
} catch (e) { pm.variables.set('signedAssertion', ''); console.log('assertion signing unavailable: ' + e.message); }
